turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey, how's your day been so far?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our wooden kitchen worktop is stained and cut up, and I'm deciding what to do.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me lay out all the options first. Don't interrupt.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sand it all the way down and re-oil it, which takes a whole weekend.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just sand the worst spots and live with a slightly patchy look.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Cover it with a stick on vinyl wrap that looks like marble.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or bite the bullet and replace it with a new laminate one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's all I've got. Which would you choose?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If the cuts are shallow, sanding the whole thing is the best value. Spot sanding often looks worse than leaving it, because the fresh patches stand out. I'd skip the vinyl near any heat or water.
